We bring skills in programming,problem-solving, and creative thinking. We welcome members with interests in Python, AI/ML, data science,astronomy, and software development who are eager to collaborate and build an impactful solution.
summary:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive web-based platform designed to identify and evaluate potentially safe landing locations on the Moon. It addresses the challenges of lunar landing site selection by combining lunar terrain visualization, scientific data analysis, and intelligent decision-support techniques.

The platform aims to analyze important factors such as surface slope, elevation, craters, terrain roughness, and environmental conditions like temperature and solar illumination. Users can explore lunar regions, select coordinates, visualize terrain characteristics, and compare potential landing locations based on multiple parameters.

By integrating NASA's lunar datasets with interactive 2D/3D visualization and AI-assisted analysis, our project aims to simplify complex lunar geographical information and support more informed landing-site decisions. This is important for improving our understanding of lunar surface conditions and supporting future lunar exploration missions.
details:
Lunar Surface Explorer is a research prototype designed to help users explore and compare potential lunar landing areas near the Moon's south pole.

How does it work?

The proposed application provides an interactive lunar map and a terrain-based comparison of candidate landing locations. It uses NASA's Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) data to examine elevation, surface slope, and elevation uncertainty. Three candidate landing footprints are compared using a weighted terrain scoring method. A lower score indicates a more favourable option within the selected comparison.

Benefits and Impact

The project aims to make lunar terrain information easier to understand and help users identify potentially promising landing areas. It provides a visual and data-driven approach to preliminary lunar landing-site exploration.

Tools and Technologies

The project uses web development technologies, data visualization techniques, NASA lunar terrain datasets, and computational analysis for terrain comparison. AI-assisted tools were also used during the development and documentation process.

Creativity and Innovation

Our approach combines lunar terrain visualization with quantitative comparison in one platform. Instead of examining coordinates alone, users can compare multiple terrain measurements and understand why one candidate ranks ahead of another.

Current Development Stage

The project is currently a research prototype. Detailed terrain screening is demonstrated for one region near the lunar south pole. Expanding terrain coverage and adding further environmental analysis are planned future improvements.

This project is intended for preliminary research and educational exploration, not actual spacecraft landing guidance or safety certification.
